theme: The Tabernacle is built, every detail according to the pattern
readingInstruction: Read Exodus 36:1-38:31. After the long instructions, you now watch the work being done. Much of the text repeats what you read in chapters 25 to 31. As you read, notice what the repetition is meant to show.
settingTheScene: The instructions are complete and the golden calf has been dealt with. Now the people build the tabernacle. Bezalel, Oholiab, and the skilled workers receive the offerings and do the work. The text slows down and tells again, almost word for word, what was commanded earlier, this time in the past tense. The point is not to tell you something new. It is to show you that the work was done exactly as God said.
observation: The people bring so much that Moses has to restrain them: “The people bring much more than enough for doing the work” (36:5-6).
The craftsmen make the curtains, the frames, and the veil, using the same materials and dimensions as in chapters 25 and 26 (36:8-38).
Bezalel makes the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altar of incense, and the oil and incense (37:1-29).
The bronze basin is made from “the mirrors of the ministering women who ministered in the entrance of the tent of meeting” (38:8).
The bronze altar, the courtyard, and its pillars are made (38:1-20).
The total of the gold, silver, and bronze is carefully recorded (38:21-31).
The silver from the census, a half shekel per person, is used to make the bases for the frames and veil (38:25-28).
Bezalel does “all that the LORD commanded Moses” (38:22).
interpretation:
It is easy to skim a chapter that repeats itself. Do not. The repetition is the message. When Exodus 36 to 38 says that the craftsmen made it “as the LORD had commanded Moses,” it is saying that Israel, who failed so badly at the golden calf, now obeys. The pattern of rebellion, intercession, forgiveness, and renewed obedience is one of the most important in the book.

The second thing to note is the generosity. The people bring so much that Moses has to stop them. This is the opposite of the golden calf. At the calf, they gave their gold to make an idol. Now they give their gold, silver, and bronze for the worship of the true God. The same people, the same metals, a different heart.

The third thing is the humble detail of the bronze basin. It is made from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent. Someone gave up a prized personal possession so that the priests could be washed. It is not a large gift, and yet it is recorded forever. God notices what we give, and he does not forget.

The fourth is the use of the census silver. The ransom money, paid equally by each person, forms the foundation of the sanctuary. The bases that hold the whole tent up are made of redemption money. It is a quiet picture of the way God’s dwelling place stands on atonement. The whole structure rests on the fact that each person has been ransomed.

Finally, the long accounts of metal remind you that the tabernacle was real, tangible, and costly. It was not a spiritual idea. It was built with real labor and real gifts, by people who gave their time and skill.
connection: Paul calls the church God’s building and says that “Jesus Christ himself being the cornerstone” holds it together (Ephesians 2:20-22). Peter says we are “living stones” being built into a spiritual house (1 Peter 2:5). The foundation is the ransom paid by Christ, “a lamb without blemish or spot” (1 Peter 1:19). Paul praises generous giving as “a fragrant offering” (Philippians 4:18).
application:
Think about the difference between the golden calf and the tabernacle. Ask whether anything you give, in time, money, or talent, is going toward something that cannot give life.

Give something this week, anonymously if you can, and without being asked.

Thank God that the foundation of your life with him is a ransom already paid.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for the people who give cheerfully, and ask him to make you one.
Thank him for the ransom that is the foundation of his house.
Ask him to make you a living stone in what he is building.
